it-b01-n01: Good news: Italian is written the way it sounds. Four moves, and words you half-know start landing.
it-b01-n02: First move: every vowel gets said. English eats word endings; Italian does not. Pane is PA-ne, both halves.
it-b01-p01: At the counter, order one coffee. Say every syllable. Speak now.
it-b01-n03: Second: the double consonant is real. Nono is ninth, nonno is grandfather. Hold the double a beat longer.
it-b01-p02: Order a beer, holding both double letters. Speak now.
it-b01-n04: Third: c and g go soft before e and i — ciao, gelato. Before a, o and u they stay hard.
it-b01-p03: Order a chocolate gelato. Soft g, soft c. Speak now.
it-b01-n05: Fourth: stress lands on the second-to-last syllable. When it does not, the written accent tells you.
it-b01-p04: Ask where the station is. The accent on è tells you where to land. Speak now.
it-b01-p05: Thank them. Two words, both vowels landed. Speak now.
it-b01-p06: Greet the barista before you order anything. Speak now.
it-b01-p07: Ask for water. Hold the double c in acqua’s cousin — say every vowel. Speak now.
it-b01-p08: You lost the answer. Ask them to repeat more slowly. Speak now.
it-b01-s01: Un caffè, per favore. Vorrei una birra. Dov'è la stazione? Grazie mille.
it-b01-n06: B01 done. Every vowel said, doubles held, c and g soft before e and i, stress where the accent puts it.
it-b01-q-i: A traveller orders at an Italian counter and asks for directions.
it-b02-n01: Italian courtesy is not long sentences. It is timing — the right short word, one beat before you act.
it-b02-p01: You step into a small shop in the morning. Greet the room before you look at anything. Speak now.
it-b02-n02: Buongiorno runs until mid-afternoon, then buonasera takes over. Nobody minds if you switch early.
it-b02-p02: It is now evening and you are entering a restaurant. Greet them. Speak now.
it-b02-n03: Now the body move. Permesso goes before you squeeze past someone — you announce the movement, you do not apologise for it.
it-b02-p03: A crowded bus, and your stop is next. Announce the move before you make it. Speak now.
it-b02-n04: Scusi is the other one, and it does different work: it opens a question to a stranger, or repairs a bump.
it-b02-p04: You need to stop someone on the street to ask something. Open with the right word. Speak now.
it-b02-n05: Mi dica means the floor is yours. It is not a request for your life story — say the thing you needed.
it-b02-p05: In a shop, the owner asks what you need but you are only browsing. Say so, warmly. Speak now.
it-b02-n06: Last move: closing. Arrivederci on the way out — one word, said before the door, not after it.
it-b02-p06: You have paid and are leaving. Thank them and sign off. Speak now.
it-b02-p07: Return the wish, in two words. Speak now.
it-b02-p08: Someone held a door for you. Thank them, briefly. Speak now.
it-b02-s01: Buongiorno! Permesso. Scusi, posso chiederle una cosa? Grazie, arrivederci!
it-b02-n07: B02 done. Buongiorno on the way in, permesso before the body moves, scusi to open a question, arrivederci before the door.
it-b02-q-i: A traveller enters a shop, moves through a crowd and leaves properly.
it-b03-n01: The dangerous move is the polite nod at an answer you did not catch. It buys one second and costs you the afternoon.
it-b03-r01: Allora, deve andare fino al semaforo e poi girare subito dopo il ponte.
it-b03-n02: Here is the frame: mi può, then the thing you need done. One opening, and you swap only the action.
it-b03-p01: Ask for the whole thing again, slower. Not louder — slower. Speak now.
it-b03-r02: Certo. Fino al semaforo, poi a destra.
it-b03-n03: Slower still fails when the payload is a number, a name or an address. Stop spending listening attempts on it.
it-b03-p02: Same frame, new action: ask them to write it down. Speak now.
it-b03-t02: Me lo può scrivere, per favore?
it-b03-n04: Third channel: the map. A written street name can still leave three turnings unclear — hand over the phone.
it-b03-p03: Open the map and ask them to show you the point. Speak now.
it-b03-r03: Sì, guardi: è qui, dopo la piazza.
it-b03-n05: Fourth: cut the answer down before it grows. Asking if it is far turns a paragraph into a decision.
it-b03-p04: You only need to know whether to walk. Ask if it is far. Speak now.
it-b03-n06: And the honest sentence that starts the whole ladder — say it plainly, with no apology attached.
it-b03-p05: You lost the thread. Say so, without apologising for existing. Speak now.
it-b03-p06: Set the pace for the whole conversation, not just one sentence. Speak now.
it-b03-p07: Only the number was lost, not the whole answer. Ask for just that. Speak now.
it-b03-p08: They were patient with you. Say so. Speak now.
it-b03-s01: Scusi, non ho capito. Mi può ripetere più lentamente? Me lo può scrivere, per favore?
it-b03-n07: B03 done. Mi può plus the action: slower, written, on the map. È lontano? shrinks the answer. The frame stays, the action changes.
it-b03-q-i: A traveller loses an answer and climbs the repair ladder instead of nodding.
it-b03-q01: Deve andare fino al semaforo e poi girare dopo il ponte.
it-b04-n01: Tomorrow's trip starts tonight. Four files, checked while a mistake still costs nothing to fix.
it-b04-n02: One: the passport, and your airline's own validity rule — the airline's boarding check and the border's rule are not the same thing.
it-b04-n03: Two: make the booking survive a dead phone. Save the hotel address and the return ticket somewhere that works with no signal.
it-b04-p01: You are calling the hotel before flying. Open with the job. Speak now.
it-b04-n04: A green tick inside an app is not proof. Ask for the confirmation somewhere you can keep it.
it-b04-p02: Ask them to send the confirmation by email so you can save it offline. Speak now.
it-b04-t02: Mi può mandare la conferma per email?
it-b04-n05: A hotel name is not a destination. A driver and an offline map need the full street address.
it-b04-p03: The booking shows only the hotel name. Ask for the complete address. Speak now.
it-b04-p04: You will not remember that. Ask for it in writing. Speak now.
it-b04-n06: Three: connection. Install the eSIM at home, and keep the activation steps somewhere readable without connection.
it-b04-n07: Four: two ways to pay, both tested by you. Cards decline abroad for reasons nobody explains at the counter.
it-b04-p05: Your flight lands late. Say when you arrive and check reception is open. Speak now.
it-b04-t05: Arrivo dopo le undici. La reception è aperta?
it-b04-p06: Get a phone number you can call from the airport. Speak now.
it-b04-p07: Ask them to hold the booking until you arrive. Speak now.
it-b04-p08: Close the call warmly. Speak now.
it-b04-s01: Vorrei confermare la mia prenotazione. Qual è l'indirizzo completo? Me lo può scrivere?
it-b04-n08: B04 done. Passport checked, booking confirmed and saved offline, full address in writing, connection and two payment methods tested.
it-b04-q-i: A traveller calls the hotel the night before and closes every gap.
it-b05-n01: Passport control is not an Italian exam. Three jobs only: why you came, how long, where you sleep. True answer, then stop.
it-b05-r01: Buongiorno. Qual è il motivo del viaggio?
it-b05-p01: You are travelling for a holiday. One sentence. Speak now.
it-b05-n02: Use your real number. Ten days is the rehearsal value, not a line to memorise for every trip.
it-b05-p02: Give only the duration, nothing else. Speak now.
it-b05-n03: Not the story of how you found the hotel. Name it, and let the booking you saved hold the address.
it-b05-p03: Say where you are staying, briefly. Speak now.
it-b05-p04: Hand over the offline confirmation without adding a speech. Speak now.
it-b05-n04: Eccola is the whole sentence. Two syllables and an outstretched hand beat a paragraph every time.
it-b05-p05: You did not catch the question. Ask cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
it-b05-t05: Scusi, non ho capito la domanda.
it-b05-p06: Say you are travelling alone. Speak now.
it-b05-p07: They ask if you are visiting other cities. Answer briefly and truthfully. Speak now.
it-b05-p08: Close it in two words and move on. Speak now.
it-b05-s01: Sono in vacanza. Dieci giorni. In un hotel a Roma. Sì, eccola.
it-b05-n05: B05 done. Purpose, duration, where you sleep. Short is not evasive — short means the answer matched the question.
it-b05-q-i: A traveller answers passport control in three short sentences.
it-b05-q01: Qual è il motivo del viaggio?
it-b06-n01: Your first hour is a run of small permissions. The rules change building to building, so the useful skill is asking, not knowing.
it-b06-n02: Here is the frame: posso, then the action. Can I — and then the job. Same opening every time.
it-b06-p01: At the airport bar you want water and all you have is plastic. Ask. Speak now.
it-b06-n03: The frame holds; only the action changes. Same four words, completely different problem.
it-b06-p02: The toilets are past a staffed barrier. Ask whether you may use them. Speak now.
it-b06-p03: Your pickup is late and you want a visible spot near staff. Ask. Speak now.
it-b06-n04: Si accomodi means go ahead, sit, help yourself. You will hear it constantly — it is a yes with a welcome attached.
it-b06-p04: Battery nearly dead, and there is a socket by the wall. Ask. Speak now.
it-b06-p05: You need both hands free at the desk. Ask about the suitcase. Speak now.
it-b06-n05: And when the answer is no, it usually comes with the reason and the alternative. Listen past the no.
it-b06-r03: Qui no, ma c'è il deposito bagagli al piano di sotto.
it-b06-p06: Your eSIM is not connecting. Ask about the wifi. Speak now.
it-b06-p07: Open a question with the same frame, politely. Speak now.
it-b06-p08: They sorted you out. Thank them properly. Speak now.
it-b06-s01: Posso pagare con la carta? Posso usare il bagno? Posso aspettare qui?
it-b06-n06: B06 done. Posso plus the action covers pay, toilet, wait, charge and bag — five problems, one frame, four words each.
it-b06-q-i: A traveller handles five small permissions with one opening.
it-b07-n01: Getting from the airport to the bed is one decision repeated: find the official thing, then name where you are going.
it-b07-n02: The frame is dov'è, plus the place. Where is — and then the thing you need to reach.
it-b07-t01: Scusi, dov'è la fermata dei taxi?
it-b07-p01: Walk past the person offering you a ride and ask staff for the official rank. Speak now.
it-b07-n03: Same frame, different place. This is the one that gets you out of any building you are turned around in.
it-b07-p02: You have lost the exit entirely. Ask. Speak now.
it-b07-n04: In the car, give the address the way you saved it in B04 — street, number, city. Show the screen while you say it.
it-b07-p03: You are in the taxi. Give the destination, showing the saved address. Speak now.
it-b07-n05: Now close the ride before you open the hotel. Stop the car where you can actually get out with the bag.
it-b07-p04: The hotel door is right there. Tell the driver this spot is fine. Speak now.
it-b07-p05: Ask for the receipt before you get out. Speak now.
it-b07-p06: Before setting off, ask roughly what it will cost. Speak now.
it-b07-p07: You have decided on the train instead. Ask for the station. Speak now.
it-b07-p08: Same frame, and the smallest need there is. Ask where the toilet is. Speak now.
it-b07-s01: Dov'è la fermata dei taxi? A questo indirizzo, per favore. Qui va bene, grazie.
it-b07-n06: B07 done. Dov'è finds the rank, the exit, the station and the toilet. The address goes on the screen, and qui va bene ends the ride.
it-b07-q-i: A traveller finds the official taxi rank and closes the ride properly.
it-b07-q01: Scusi, dov’è la fermata dei taxi?
it-b08-n01: Ask where something is and you get three streets and a hand wave. Start smaller — ask whether it exists at all.
it-b08-n02: The frame is c'è, plus the thing. The answer is yes or no, and yes or no fits in your head.
it-b08-p01: You need medicine but do not know if this street has a pharmacy. Ask the yes-or-no question first. Speak now.
it-b08-n03: The opening holds; the thing changes. You want any cash machine, not a particular one.
it-b08-p02: You need cash. Keep the frame, swap the thing. Speak now.
it-b08-n04: Bancomat is the word — it is what the machine is called, and asking for an ATM will slow you down.
it-b08-p03: Simplest possible existence question, in a café. Speak now.
it-b08-r02: Sì, la password è sul tavolo.
it-b08-n05: Now the answer that is too large. Do not ask for the same paragraph again — collapse it into distance.
it-b08-r03: Allora, prende la seconda a destra, poi sempre dritto fino alla chiesa, e dopo la piazza gira a sinistra.
it-b08-p04: You lost the middle. Ask only whether it is far. Speak now.
it-b08-p05: Ten minutes still leaves the first turn unclear. Move it to the map. Speak now.
it-b08-p06: Same frame, completely different scene: a busy restaurant. Speak now.
it-b08-p07: You missed the connection. Ask whether another exists. Speak now.
it-b08-p08: They walked you through it patiently. Thank them. Speak now.
it-b08-s01: C'è una farmacia qui vicino? È lontano? Mi può mostrare sulla mappa?
it-b08-n06: B08 done. C'è asks whether it exists, è lontano? shrinks a paragraph, and the map takes over when words stop moving your feet.
it-b08-q-i: A traveller shrinks a three-street answer into one usable move.
it-b08-q02: Sì, prende la seconda a destra, poi sempre dritto fino alla chiesa.
it-b09-n01: Every guidebook says stamp your ticket in Italy. That advice is now half right, and knowing which half saves you fifty euros.
it-b09-r01: Il regionale per Firenze parte dal binario sette.
it-b09-n02: First, buy for the destination. Un biglietto per, then the city — that is the whole transaction.
it-b09-p01: At the counter, ask for one ticket to Florence. Speak now.
it-b09-t01: Un biglietto per Firenze, per favore.
it-b09-n03: If it is digital, it validates itself at the departure time you chose. No machine, no stamp — but the QR has to be showable.
it-b09-n04: If it is paper, the old rule stands: stamp it before boarding. Unstamped paper is a fine of fifty euros plus the fare.
it-b09-p02: You are holding a paper ticket and are not sure. Ask whether you have to stamp it. Speak now.
it-b09-r02: Sì, quello di carta sì. Alla macchinetta verde.
it-b09-p03: Now find the machine. Use the frame from B07. Speak now.
it-b09-n05: Then the platform. Binario is the word, and the number is on the screen — you do not have to produce it from memory.
it-b09-p04: Ask where platform seven is. Speak now.
it-b09-p05: The train is at the platform. Before boarding, confirm it goes where you think. Speak now.
it-b09-p06: Ask what time it leaves, to check against your ticket. Speak now.
it-b09-p07: Ask whether you have to change trains on the way. Speak now.
it-b09-p08: The inspector is coming and your phone is asleep. Say the ticket is on your phone. Speak now.
it-b09-t08: Il biglietto è sul telefono, un momento.
it-b09-s01: Un biglietto per Firenze, per favore. Devo convalidare il biglietto? Dov'è il binario sette?
it-b09-n06: B09 done. Digital validates itself, paper needs the green machine, binario is the platform, and the QR must be showable.
it-b09-q-i: A traveller buys a regional ticket and works out which validation rule applies.
it-b09-q01: Un biglietto per Firenze, per favore.
it-b09-q03: Sì, quello di carta sì. Alla macchinetta verde.
it-b10-n01: Italian signs look readable, which is the trap. Some words mean exactly what you think. A few do not, and those are the expensive ones.
it-b10-r01: Chiuso per ferie. Riapriamo il ventidue agosto.
it-b10-n02: Aperto and chiuso are the whole game. Open and closed, on every door in the country.
it-b10-r02: Orario continuato. Aperto tutti i giorni.
it-b10-n03: Now the false friends. Camera is a room, not a camera. Fattoria is a farm, not a factory. Morbido is soft, not morbid.
it-b10-p01: The sign is long and you only need one thing. Ask whether the place is open. Speak now.
it-b10-r03: Riservato ai clienti. Guasto, fuori servizio.
it-b10-n04: Guasto is broken. Fuori servizio is out of order. Both mean the same thing to you: find the other machine.
it-b10-p02: You are looking at a word you do not know. Ask what it means. Speak now.
it-b10-n05: Doors: spingere is push, tirare is pull. Entrata in, uscita out. Vietato means forbidden, and it is always serious.
it-b10-p03: The hours are handwritten and unreadable. Ask when they open. Speak now.
it-b10-r04: Alle sedici. Ora facciamo la pausa.
it-b10-n06: Sedici is sixteen — the twenty-four hour clock. Written hours are almost always in it, spoken ones often are too.
it-b10-p04: Ask whether there is an afternoon break, using the frame from B08. Speak now.
it-b10-p05: This door says uscita. Ask where the way in is. Speak now.
it-b10-p06: The sign says riservato and you are not sure it applies to you. Ask. Speak now.
it-b10-p07: They read the sign aloud too fast. Ask them to write the time down. Speak now.
it-b10-p08: Confirm the closed day so you do not walk back for nothing. Speak now.
it-b10-s01: Scusi, è aperto? Cosa vuol dire questo? A che ora aprite?
it-b10-n07: B10 done. Aperto and chiuso, guasto and vietato, spingere and tirare — and cosa vuol dire questo for everything else.
it-b10-q-i: A traveller works out whether a shop is open, and when it will be.
it-b10-q01: Chiuso per ferie. Riapriamo il ventidue agosto.
it-b10-q03: Alle sedici. Ora facciamo la pausa.
it-b11-n01: The first round is where prices stop being obvious. There are two legal prices, and nobody says which one you picked.
it-b11-n02: The frame is quanto costa, plus the thing. How much is — and then whatever you are about to commit to.
it-b11-t01: Quanto costa un caffè al tavolo?
it-b11-p01: You are about to sit down in a famous square. Ask first. Speak now.
it-b11-r01: Al tavolo sono sei euro, al banco uno e trenta.
it-b11-n03: That gap is legal, and both tariffs must be displayed. You are choosing, whether you know it or not.
it-b11-p02: Now ask the counter price, the other half of the choice. Speak now.
it-b11-n04: Un caffè means an espresso. If you want the long one, say caffè lungo — otherwise you get the small strong one.
it-b11-p03: Order at the counter: a coffee and a glass of water. Speak now.
it-b11-t03: Un caffè e un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.
it-b11-p04: Two things, one total. Ask for the whole amount. Speak now.
it-b11-r02: Sono due e cinquanta. Prima paghi alla cassa.
it-b11-n05: In many bars you pay at the till first and take the receipt to the counter. If someone points at the cassa, that is what is happening.
it-b11-p05: You have decided the table is worth it. Ask about one outside. Speak now.
it-b11-p06: At a market stall, pointing at something with no price tag. Speak now.
it-b11-p07: You are unsure whether to pay here or at the till. Ask. Speak now.
it-b11-p08: Ask for the receipt, which the bar has to give you anyway. Speak now.
it-b11-s01: Quanto costa un caffè al tavolo? E al banco, quanto costa? Quanto costa in tutto?
it-b11-n06: B11 done. Quanto costa covers the table, the counter, the total and the stall — before you commit.
it-b11-q-i: A traveller finds out about the second price before sitting down.
it-b11-q01: Quanto costa un caffè al tavolo?
it-b11-q02: Al tavolo sono sei euro, al banco uno e trenta.
it-b11-q04: Sono due e cinquanta. Prima paghi alla cassa.
it-b12-n01: Most of what you want to say at a table is not a new dish. It is a dish on the menu, minus one thing.
it-b12-n02: The frame is senza, plus the thing you do not want. Without — and then the ingredient.
it-b12-p01: The salad is right except for one ingredient. Subtract it. Speak now.
it-b12-n03: The frame does not care what follows. Any ingredient, any drink, any dish — the word in front never changes.
it-b12-p02: Same frame, a drink this time: no ice. Speak now.
it-b12-p03: Ask whether there is a gluten-free version. Speak now.
it-b12-n04: Senza glutine is on packaging and menus everywhere. It is the one subtraction Italy already had a printed label for.
it-b12-n05: The opposite direction works too. Con adds, and più asks for more of something already there.
it-b12-p04: Add something instead of removing it: with lemon. Speak now.
it-b12-p05: Ask for a little more bread. Speak now.
it-b12-t05: Un po' più di pane, per favore.
it-b12-p06: The pasta comes with cheese on top and you would rather it did not. Speak now.
it-b12-r02: Il formaggio è già dentro. Le faccio un altro primo?
it-b12-n06: Sometimes the answer is no, and the reason is that it was cooked in. Take the alternative they offer — that is the sentence doing its job.
it-b12-p07: Ask whether they can do it without butter. Speak now.
it-b12-p08: You want the flat kind of bottled water, not the fizzy kind. Order it. Speak now.
it-b12-s01: Senza cipolla, per favore. Senza ghiaccio, per favore. Acqua senza gas, per favore.
it-b12-n07: B12 done. Senza subtracts, con adds, più asks for more — and the menu stops being a fixed list.
it-b12-q-i: A traveller edits a dish on the menu instead of describing a new one.
it-b12-q04: Il formaggio è già dentro. Le faccio un altro primo?
it-b13-n01: The last part taught you to subtract politely. This one is different. An allergy is not a preference and must not sound like one.
it-b13-n02: Lead with the word allergia. It is the word that changes what happens in the kitchen, so it goes first, not last.
it-b13-t01: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave.
it-b13-p01: Say it before ordering, not after. Name it and say it is serious. Speak now.
it-b13-r01: Ho capito. Lo dico in cucina.
it-b13-n03: Lo dico in cucina is the answer you want. A warm nod without it means the message stopped at the table.
it-b13-p02: You did not hear the kitchen mentioned. Ask them to tell the kitchen. Speak now.
it-b13-t02: Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?
it-b13-n04: Now the card. Write it before the trip, in Italian, on paper and on your phone. Paper works when the battery does not.
it-b13-p03: Hand over the written card instead of repeating yourself. Speak now.
it-b13-p04: Ask directly whether the dish contains it. Speak now.
it-b13-r02: Questo no, ma è fritto nello stesso olio.
it-b13-n05: That answer is the good one. Same oil, same board, same water is the risk the menu never prints.
it-b13-p05: Ask what there is with none of it at all, using the frame from B12. Speak now.
it-b13-p06: Say what happens if you eat it, in four words. Speak now.
it-b13-p07: The worst case. Ask them to call an ambulance. Speak now.
it-b13-p08: The plate has arrived. Confirm once before the first bite. Speak now.
it-b13-s01: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave. Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?
it-b13-n06: B13 done. Allergia first, è grave second, the card third, and one confirmation before the first bite.
it-b13-q-i: A traveller makes sure an allergy reaches the kitchen, not just the table.
it-b13-q01: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave.
it-b13-q02: Ho capito. Lo dico in cucina.
it-b13-q04: Questo no, ma è fritto nello stesso olio.
it-b14-n01: The end of a meal has one sentence and two lines of reading. Get both right and the bill stops being a surprise.
it-b14-n02: The frame is mi porta, plus the thing. Bring me — and then whatever you want at the table.
it-b14-t01: Mi porta il conto, per favore?
it-b14-p01: You are ready to go. Ask for the bill. Speak now.
it-b14-n03: The bill does not arrive on its own here. Staying at the table after the plates are gone is normal, so you have to ask.
it-b14-p02: Same frame, mid-meal: ask for some water. Speak now.
it-b14-n04: Two lines to read: coperto, the cover charge, and servizio. Both are legal when the menu declared them.
it-b14-r01: Coperto due euro a persona, servizio dieci per cento.
it-b14-p03: There is a line you do not recognise. Ask what it is, at the table. Speak now.
it-b14-n05: If servizio is already on the bill, you are done. Tipping on top is not expected in Italy — rounding up is plenty.
it-b14-p04: Check the payment method before they walk away. Speak now.
it-b14-p05: You are two and want to split it. Ask. Speak now.
it-b14-p06: Ask for the receipt — they are legally obliged to issue it. Speak now.
it-b14-t06: Mi porta lo scontrino, per favore?
it-b14-p07: The total does not match. Say so calmly and ask them to check. Speak now.
it-b14-t07: Può controllare il totale, per favore?
it-b14-p08: Round up and close it warmly. Speak now.
it-b14-s01: Mi porta il conto, per favore? Scusi, cos'è questa voce? Mi porta lo scontrino, per favore?
it-b14-n06: B14 done. Mi porta brings anything to the table, coperto and servizio are legal when declared, and the scontrino is owed to you.
it-b14-q-i: A traveller asks for the bill, reads the two extra lines, and takes the receipt.
it-b14-q01: Mi porta il conto, per favore?
it-b14-q02: Coperto due euro a persona, servizio dieci per cento.
it-b14-q04: Mi porta lo scontrino, per favore?
it-b15-n01: A shop is four questions long. How much, do you have my size, can I try it, and can I change it.
it-b15-n02: Dica pure means tell me what you need. Greet first — in a small shop, walking in silently reads as odd.
it-b15-p01: You want to browse without committing. Say so warmly. Speak now.
it-b15-p02: Nothing on this one has a tag. Use the frame from B11. Speak now.
it-b15-p03: It is close but tight. Ask about the next size up. Speak now.
it-b15-r02: Solo la media e la large. Vuole provarla?
it-b15-p04: Ask to try it on, using the frame from B06. Speak now.
it-b15-n03: Now the question people skip. Ask about changing it before you pay, not after — the answer differs by shop.
it-b15-p05: Ask whether you can exchange it if it does not fit. Speak now.
it-b15-t05: Posso cambiarla se non va bene?
it-b15-r03: Entro otto giorni, con lo scontrino.
it-b15-n04: With the receipt — again. In shops, at meals, in taxis, the scontrino is the thing that makes anything afterwards possible.
it-b15-p06: You like the shape, not the colour. Ask. Speak now.
it-b15-p07: Ask them to bring you a bag, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
it-b15-t07: Mi porta una borsa, per favore?
it-b15-p08: You have decided not to buy. Leave without buying, warmly. Speak now.
it-b15-s01: Quanto costa questa? Posso provarla? Posso cambiarla se non va bene?
it-b15-n05: B15 done. Greet, ask the price, try it, ask about changing it — and ci penso lets you leave without buying.
it-b15-q-i: A traveller finishes a purchase without leaving a question for later.
it-b15-q03: Posso cambiarla se non va bene?
it-b15-q04: Entro otto giorni, con lo scontrino.
it-b16-n01: Check-in is thirty seconds where everything is still adjustable. Spend it asking, not confirming what you already booked.
it-b16-p01: Confirm the booking, briefly, with the name. Speak now.
it-b16-t01: Sì, ho una prenotazione a nome Rossi.
it-b16-n02: Now ask. A quieter room costs the hotel nothing if one is free, and costs you a week of sleep if you do not ask.
it-b16-p02: The street outside is loud. Ask, using the frame from B08. Speak now.
it-b16-r02: Le do una all'ultimo piano, sul cortile.
it-b16-n03: Camera is the room, not the device. Sul cortile means courtyard-facing, which is the quiet side of almost any Italian building.
it-b16-p03: Your flight is at night. Ask about a later checkout now, not on the last morning. Speak now.
it-b16-t03: Posso fare il check-out più tardi?
it-b16-p04: Ask what time breakfast is, so you do not miss it on day one. Speak now.
it-b16-t04: A che ora è la colazione?
it-b16-n04: Only now the complaints. Name the thing that does not work and stop — no adjectives, no apology, no story.
it-b16-p05: The air conditioning is dead. Say it plainly. Speak now.
it-b16-n05: Non funziona is the whole complaint. Swap the noun in front and it covers the shower, the wifi, the lift, the key.
it-b16-p06: Same sentence, different noun: the wifi. Speak now.
it-b16-p07: The room is cold. Ask for another blanket, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
it-b16-t07: Mi porta un'altra coperta, per favore?
it-b16-p08: You arrived before the room is ready. Ask about the bags. Speak now.
it-b16-s01: C'è una camera più tranquilla? Posso fare il check-out più tardi? L'aria condizionata non funziona.
it-b16-n06: B16 done. Ask for the quieter room and the later checkout first. Non funziona handles everything that breaks after.
it-b16-q-i: A traveller spends the thirty seconds at the desk on the things that are still adjustable.
it-b16-q02: Le do una all'ultimo piano, sul cortile.
it-b16-q03: Posso fare il check-out più tardi?
it-b17-n01: This is the one part of the module that is purely defensive. It exists so that a bad night is short instead of long.
it-b17-n02: The green cross is the pharmacy. Inside, name the symptom — you are not expected to name the medicine.
it-b17-t01: Ho mal di testa da ieri.
it-b17-p01: Say what hurts and since when. Two facts, no story. Speak now.
it-b17-r01: Prende altri farmaci? È allergico a qualcosa?
it-b17-n03: Mal di, plus the body part. Mal di testa, mal di gola, mal di stomaco, mal di denti. One pattern, four bad nights.
it-b17-p02: Same pattern, different body part: your throat. Speak now.
it-b17-p03: You cannot take one common ingredient. Subtract it, using the frame from B12. Speak now.
it-b17-p04: Ask whether it needs a prescription before they go and look. Speak now.
it-b17-n04: If the pharmacy is closed, read the door. The list taped inside says which one nearby is on duty tonight.
it-b17-r02: Farmacie di turno: via Garibaldi dodici, aperta fino alle otto.
it-b17-p05: Ask a passer-by which pharmacy is on duty. Speak now.
it-b17-t05: C'è una farmacia di turno qui vicino?
it-b17-n05: For an emergency, one number: one-one-two. It works from any phone in Italy, with no credit and usually with no SIM.
it-b17-p06: Someone needs help now. Ask for an ambulance. Speak now.
it-b17-p07: On the phone to one-one-two, say where you are before anything else. Speak now.
it-b17-t07: Sono in via Garibaldi, davanti alla farmacia.
it-b17-p08: Ask where the emergency department is, using the frame from B07. Speak now.
it-b17-s01: Ho mal di testa da ieri. C'è qualcosa senza aspirina? Dov'è il pronto soccorso?
it-b17-n06: B17 done. Mal di plus the body part, the duty list on the closed door, one-one-two, and pronto soccorso.
it-b17-q-i: A traveller solves a bad night instead of waiting it out.
it-b17-q01: Ho mal di testa da ieri.
it-b17-q02: Prende altri farmaci? È allergico a qualcosa?
it-b17-q04: Farmacie di turno: via Garibaldi dodici, aperta fino alle otto.
it-b18-n01: The last morning has two halves. The paperwork, which is quick, and the goodbye, which is the part you will remember.
it-b18-p01: Open the checkout in one sentence. Speak now.
it-b18-r01: Certo. Ha preso qualcosa dal frigobar?
it-b18-n02: Answer that one honestly and read the bill anyway — the tourist tax lands here, and it was never in what you prepaid.
it-b18-p02: Ask to see the itemised bill before paying. Speak now.
it-b18-p03: You have a whole day and a suitcase. Ask, with the time. Speak now.
it-b18-t03: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei?
it-b18-r02: Certo, gliela mettiamo nel deposito. Nessun problema.
it-b18-p04: Check whether the left luggage costs anything, using the frame from B11. Speak now.
it-b18-n03: Now the part that is not administration. Say something specific — specific is what separates thanks from a formula.
it-b18-p05: Tell them you were very comfortable here. Speak now.
it-b18-t05: Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto.
it-b18-p06: Name the thing that actually helped: their advice about the restaurant. Speak now.
it-b18-t06: Il ristorante che ci ha consigliato era ottimo.
it-b18-r03: Che piacere sentirlo. Torni a trovarci!
it-b18-p07: Answer that properly — say you'll be back. Speak now.
it-b18-p08: Ask them to get you a taxi to the airport, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
it-b18-t08: Mi chiama un taxi per l'aeroporto?
it-b18-s01: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei? Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto. Alla prossima!
it-b18-n04: B18 done, and ME VIRO with it. You can arrive, eat, buy, sleep, get help, and leave in a way people remember.
it-b18-q-i: A traveller closes the trip properly rather than just leaving.
it-b18-q02: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei?
it-b18-q03: Il ristorante che ci ha consigliato era ottimo.
it-b18-q04: Che piacere sentirlo. Torni a trovarci!
it-i06-n01: The moment you can say what you did yesterday, you stop being a person who orders things and start being someone with a trip.
it-i06-n02: Verb one: sono andato. I went. Sono andata if you are a woman — the ending agrees, and nobody minds if you miss it.
it-i06-p01: Say where you went yesterday. One place, one sentence. Speak now.
it-i06-n03: Verb two: ho mangiato. I ate. This one takes ho, not sono, and that difference is the whole grammar you need here.
it-i06-p02: Say what you ate. Name the dish, not the restaurant. Speak now.
it-i06-t02: Ho mangiato la bistecca alla fiorentina.
it-i06-r02: Ah, quella vera! E dove, scusa?
it-i06-n04: Verb three is the one that keeps the conversation alive: mi è piaciuto. I liked it. Literally, it pleased me.
it-i06-p03: Say you liked it very much. Speak now.
it-i06-p04: String two of them together — where and what. Speak now.
it-i06-t04: Sono andato al mercato e ho comprato del formaggio.
it-i06-n05: Notice the pattern: movement takes sono, doing-something-to-a-thing takes ho. That covers most of what you will want to say.
it-i06-p05: Say you walked a lot. Speak now.
it-i06-p06: Say what surprised you, so the story has a point. Speak now.
it-i06-r03: Eh, tutti dicono così. E domani dove andate?
it-i06-p07: Answer the tomorrow question and hand it back to them. Speak now.
it-i06-t07: Domani andiamo a Siena. Lei c'è stato?
it-i06-p08: Say the one thing you did not like, lightly. A trip with no low point sounds invented. Speak now.
it-i06-t08: Il museo, invece, non mi è piaciuto tanto.
it-i06-s01: Ieri sono andato a Firenze. Ho mangiato la bistecca alla fiorentina. Mi è piaciuto moltissimo.
it-i06-n06: I06 done. Sono andato, ho mangiato, mi è piaciuto — where, what, and how it landed. That is a story.
it-i06-q-i: A traveller turns a day into an account someone wants to continue.
it-i06-q02: Ieri sono andato a Firenze. Ho mangiato la bistecca alla fiorentina.
it-i06-q03: Ah, quella vera! E dove, scusa?
it-i06-q04: Mi è piaciuto moltissimo. Domani andiamo a Siena. Lei c'è stato?
it-i07-n01: Two sentences, opposite jobs, same rule: name the thing. Vague praise dies at the table and vague complaints get an apology instead of a fix.
it-i07-n02: Praise first. Tutto buono is polite noise. Name the dish and it becomes a message someone will actually repeat.
it-i07-t01: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco.
it-i07-p01: Praise one dish by name and send it to the kitchen. Speak now.
it-i07-r01: Glielo dico subito. È mia madre che cucina.
it-i07-n03: Buonissimo, ottimo, squisito. Any of the three is stronger than very good, and all three are ordinary words here.
it-i07-p02: Praise the place rather than the plate. Speak now.
it-i07-n04: Now the complaint. State the fact, no adjectives, no apology. Scusi, plus what is wrong, and then stop talking.
it-i07-p03: The dish arrived cold. Say only that. Speak now.
it-i07-r02: Mi dispiace tantissimo, glielo cambio subito.
it-i07-n05: That worked because there was a fact in it. Adding it is a shame or I am so sorry to bother you gives them nothing to act on.
it-i07-p04: Wrong dish entirely. Say what you ordered instead. Speak now.
it-i07-t04: Scusi, io avevo ordinato il pesce.
it-i07-p05: The glass is chipped. Ask for another, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
it-i07-t05: Mi porta un altro bicchiere, per favore?
it-i07-p06: It has been forty minutes. Ask about it without accusing anyone. Speak now.
it-i07-p07: They fixed it immediately. Close the loop so it does not stay awkward. Speak now.
it-i07-p08: Say you will come back — the strongest compliment there is. Speak now.
it-i07-s01: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco. Scusi, questo è freddo. Grazie, gentilissimo.
it-i07-n06: I07 done. Name the dish to praise it, name the fact to fix it, and close warmly either way.
it-i07-q-i: A traveller sends a compliment to the kitchen and gets a cold dish replaced.
it-i07-q01: La pasta era buonissima, complimenti al cuoco.
it-i07-q02: Glielo dico subito. È mia madre che cucina.
it-i07-q04: Mi dispiace tantissimo, glielo cambio subito.
it-i05-n01: Nearly every conversation you have in Italy opens with the same five questions. That is not a limitation — it is a script you can learn.
it-i05-p01: Answer question one. Give a place they can picture. Speak now.
it-i05-t01: Siamo di Boston, negli Stati Uniti.
it-i05-n02: Question two is always how long. Give the number and the unit, the same way you did at the border.
it-i05-p02: Say how long you are staying, and add where you go next. Speak now.
it-i05-t02: Dieci giorni. Poi andiamo in Sicilia.
it-i05-r02: È la prima volta in Italia?
it-i05-p03: Answer question three and give them something to react to. Speak now.
it-i05-t03: No, la seconda. La prima volta ero a Roma.
it-i05-n03: Question four is what you do. Two words is a complete answer — nobody is asking for your career.
it-i05-p04: Say what you do, briefly. Speak now.
it-i05-n04: Question five is the one that matters: do you like it here. Answer with a specific, and the conversation opens.
it-i05-p05: Say what you like, naming one concrete thing. Speak now.
it-i05-t05: Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati.
it-i05-r03: Allora domani deve andare a quello di Sant'Ambrogio. Meno turisti.
it-i05-p06: Turn it around — ask them the question they asked you. Speak now.
it-i05-p07: You lost the question entirely. Stay in the conversation instead of leaving it. Speak now.
it-i05-t07: Scusi, mi sono perso. Può ripetere?
it-i05-p08: You have to go, and you want the door left open. Speak now.
it-i05-t08: È stato un piacere. Magari ci vediamo domani.
it-i05-s01: Siamo di Boston. Dieci giorni. Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati. E lei è di qui?
it-i05-n05: I05 done. Where from, how long, first time, what you do, do you like it — and then one question back.
it-i05-q-i: A traveller stays in the conversation and walks away with a recommendation.
it-i05-q01: Di dove siete? È la prima volta in Italia?
it-i05-q02: Siamo di Boston. No, la seconda.
it-i05-q03: Mi piace tantissimo, soprattutto i mercati.
it-i05-q04: Allora domani deve andare a quello di Sant'Ambrogio. Meno turisti.
it-i08-n01: An invitation home is the best thing that can happen on this trip, and the only reason to refuse one is not knowing how it works.
it-i08-r01: Domenica venite a pranzo da noi. Alle una.
it-i08-p01: Accept warmly and immediately. Speak now.
it-i08-n02: Then ask what to bring. The answer is usually nothing, and you bring something anyway — that exchange is part of the form.
it-i08-p02: Ask what you can bring. Speak now.
it-i08-r02: Ma niente, che dice! Portate solo voi stessi.
it-i08-n03: That is not an instruction. Bring dessert from a good pastry shop, or flowers, or wine — something for the table.
it-i08-p03: You arrive holding something. Hand it over. Speak now.
it-i08-t03: Ho portato il dolce, spero vada bene.
it-i08-n04: At the table, wait to be placed. Seats at an Italian family table are not neutral, and someone will tell you where to go.
it-i08-p04: Ask where you should sit rather than choosing. Speak now.
it-i08-n05: The toast is a formula, not a speech. Glasses up, eyes on each person, cin cin or salute. That is the whole thing.
it-i08-p05: Raise your glass and say the formula. Speak now.
it-i08-p06: Praise the food to the person who cooked it, by name of dish. Speak now.
it-i08-r03: Ne prenda ancora un po', su. Ce n'è tanto.
it-i08-p07: Accept a small amount and be honest about your limit. Speak now.
it-i08-t07: Solo un pochino, grazie. È troppo buono.
it-i08-p08: The coffee is finished and it is time. Leave properly. Speak now.
it-i08-t08: Vi ringraziamo di cuore, è stato bellissimo.
it-i08-s01: Ho portato il dolce, spero vada bene. Dove mi metto? Cin cin! Vi ringraziamo di cuore.
it-i08-n06: I08 done. Say yes, bring something, wait to be seated, raise the glass, and go when the coffee is done.
it-i08-q-i: A traveller accepts an invitation and gets the whole arc right.
it-i08-q01: Domenica venite a pranzo da noi. Alle una.
it-i08-q03: Ma niente, che dice! Portate solo voi stessi.
it-i08-q04: Ho portato il dolce, spero vada bene.
